item.text:
**8B.7 Outcome Direction, Abiy Ahmed, 2024**

**Overall read:** Mixed. The strongest positive movement is in the macroeconomic track and some targeted service-delivery areas. But broad welfare, conflict exposure, and civic-freedom indicators did not move cleanly in the claimed direction, and several worsened materially. The result is best read as partial implementation with severe offsetting harms.

- **The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia: First Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement** — IMF — 2024-11-04 — [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/11/04/the-federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia-first-review-under-the-extended-credit-facility-557019) — The IMF said Ethiopia’s reform program was advancing well, all quantitative performance criteria were met, four of five structural benchmarks were met, and the exchange-rate transition was narrowing the parallel-market gap. This is strong evidence that the macro package moved in the direction Abiy said he wanted. **QIDs:** 8B.7, 8B.6

- **Ethiopia | Data** — World Bank — 2024 — [URL](https://data.worldbank.org/country/Ethiopia?view=chart) — GDP growth was 7.6% in 2024, while inflation remained high at 21.0% and unemployment was still elevated. This is positive on growth and stabilization, but it is only a partial success because price pressure remained severe. **QIDs:** 8B.7

- **World Bank backs Ethiopia's reforms to promote sustainable and inclusive growth, enhance resilience, and take climate action** — World Bank — 2024-07-30 — [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/07/30/world-bank-backs-ethiopia-s-reforms-to-promote-sustainable-and-inclusive-afe-growth) — The reform package explicitly aimed to improve financial stability, fiscal transparency, public-spending effectiveness, SOE performance, and social safety nets. This supports a directionally positive reading for the economic trajectory, though it is still mostly program/output evidence rather than final household outcomes. **QIDs:** 8B.7, 8B.6

- **Ethiopia launches inclusive ID system for refugees, boosts access to national services** — UNHCR Africa — 2024-03-07 — [URL](https://www.unhcr.org/africa/news/press-releases/ethiopia-launches-inclusive-id-system-refugees-boosts-access-national-services) — The RRS, NID program, and UNHCR rolled out digital refugee IDs to improve access to services and reduce duplication. This is concrete evidence of targeted administrative outcomes moving in an inclusion direction. **QIDs:** 8B.7, 8B.6

- **Building a strong foundation to improve learning outcomes in AFE Ethiopia** — World Bank — 2024-09-05 — [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/09/05/building-a-strong-foundation-to-improve-learning-outcomes-in-afe-ethiopia) — The education program trained over 102,000 teachers and reported improved girls’ enrollment and refugee-school support in disadvantaged regions. This is one of the clearest positive outcome indicators for a claimed human-capital agenda. **QIDs:** 8B.7, 8B.6

- **Ethiopia and Somalia Declaration** — Republic of Türkiye Directorate of Communications — 2024-12-12 — [URL](https://www.iletisim.gov.tr/English/haberler/detay/ethiopia-somalia-ankara-declaration-under-facilitation-of-republic-of-turkiye) — The communiqué said Ethiopia and Somalia reaffirmed sovereignty, set aside disputes, and agreed to cooperate. This is a real late-year de-escalation outcome, and it moves in the direction of Abiy’s public peace claims. **QIDs:** 8B.7, 8B.5

- **Ethiopia Poverty and Equity Brief : October 2024** — World Bank — 2024-10-01 — [URL](https://documents.worldbank.org/pt/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099729001032529868) — The World Bank said living standards deteriorated across the country because of COVID-19, the Tigray conflict, Ukraine spillovers, droughts, and inflation, and that poverty was expected to have increased significantly since 2016. This is the strongest negative outcome evidence against a broad “things got better” claim. **QIDs:** 8B.7

- **World Report 2024: Ethiopia** — Human Rights Watch — 2024-01-12 — [URL](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia) — HRW reported a coordinated food-aid diversion scheme that caused WFP and USAID to halt aid, severely restricting food access for about 20 million people. That is strong negative evidence on lived welfare outcomes. **QIDs:** 8B.7, 8B.6

- **Ethiopia: Mass arbitrary detentions in Amhara region deepen erosion of rule of law** — Amnesty International — 2024-10-01 — [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/10/ethiopia-mass-arbitrary-detentions-in-amhara-region-deepen-erosion-of-rule-of-law/) — Amnesty said the army and police detained hundreds without warrants or timely court appearance, with witnesses describing “lists” and mass roundups. This is clear evidence that domestic control outcomes moved in the wrong direction. **QIDs:** 8B.7, 8B.5

- **Ethiopia military executes dozens in Amhara Region** — Human Rights Watch — 2024-04-04 — [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/04/ethiopia-military-executes-dozens-amhara-region) — HRW said Ethiopian forces summarily killed dozens of civilians in Merawi. This is a severe negative outcome indicator for civilian protection and state violence. **QIDs:** 8B.7, 8B.5

- **Landlocked Ethiopia signs pact to use Somaliland's Red Sea port** — Reuters, republished by MarketScreener — 2024-01-01 — [URL](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Landlocked-Ethiopia-signs-pact-to-use-Somaliland-s-Red-Sea-port-45654814/) — The Berbera MOU tied port access to possible naval use and possible recognition/concessions, and it was widely treated as destabilizing. This is negative on the claimed goal of safer regional outcomes, although the year ended with partial de-escalation. **QIDs:** 8B.7, 8B.5

**Search gap**
- I found strong sectoral outcome movement in macro stabilization and some service-delivery/inclusion programs.
- I did not find a clean, broad national indicator showing that ordinary living standards, security, and civic freedom improved together by year-end.
- The evidence instead splits: economic indicators and some program outputs improved, while conflict, food access, detention, and civil-space indicators worsened or stayed highly negative.
